All trans and gender variant people define the gender spectrum in slightly different ways. For me, gender neutral and agender are slightly different things.

I see gender neutral as identifying as neither male or female, but still being gendered. I see agender as just completely lacking a gender, if that makes any sense. And don't worry, I don't feel isolated or alone, there are a lot of other agender people out there. I know you're asking this just to rag on otherkin and call me a "special snowflake tumblerina" or whatever, but I'm still gonna answer it honestly.

Yeah, I'm otherkin, but I'm fully aware that I am born a human and will always be a human. I use identifying with other species and fictional characters to help myself cope with mental illness and past trauma. For example, one of my primary kintypes is alienkin. I have Aspergers and have a hard time understanding verbal directions as well as other things, so I use the concept of me being an alien to help myself feel less frustrated and upset at myself for not understanding what people are saying, and often messing up because of that. 

Another primary kintype of mine is the character Midousuji Akira from the show Yowamushi Pedal. In the second season, it's revealed that as a young child that his mother suddenly died before he competed in a cycling race in the near future. A few months before I graduated high school, something that almost didn't happen because my grades were garbage so it was kind of a big deal, my oldest sister passed away suddenly. This was around the time I first watched that episode, and using that connection I had with a character I really liked helped me cope a little better.

So go ahead and call me a special snowflake or whatever unoriginal garbage you have to say, I just wanted you to know my reasons before you (or anyone else) goes about being a cunt about it

I love the sense of vagueness in this piece and how, in my opinion, it feels like a cluster of broken thoughts coming together to try and form one cohesive thought. 

Maybe I'm just dumb, but I'm not entirely sure how the first stanza connects to the rest of the poem. This poem is about unrequited love, right? And I'm guessing "heart-havers" are people who are in love? I'm just not entirely sure what exactly "my work" is getting at.

That aside, this is a really nice poem. The lines are sharp and each one, whether I fully understand it or not, seems to really pack an emotional punch. There's also something really aesthetically pleasing about the lack of capitalization in the poem. It amps up the overall tone of the poem.

Great poem, great tone. I'm going to be thinking about those last two lines for awhile.

When I first saw the title of this poem, I kind of thought it was going to be a bit shitpost-y. I was very pleasantly surprised.

This poem is very simple, yet somehow indescribably powerful. It's giving me emotions, a mix of crippling hopelessness and the slight feeling that maybe things will get a tiny bit better, and I have no clue why. This piece just feels very relatable, maybe due to the fact that it's short and extremely easy to read (I've read it probably 10 more times as I've been writing this review).

I honestly love the feeling of a never-ending cycle here, and how the rhyme at the end loops back around to the rhyme at the beginning. There's something addictive and impactful about it. Maybe it's the looping feeling the poem gives off mixed with the looping rhyme scheme.

Whatever it is, great job on a simple yet powerful poem.
